pages.title: Eye of the Event Horizon
pages.text: Final entry in this series. A captive black hole wrapped in anchors, lenses and stabilisers - used as a computer. It simulates stars, galaxies, universes, and keeps what falls out.$(br2)$(thing)Tier 7$() machine.
Note to self: this controller is too complex for a crafting grid. It has to be built on the $(item)Femtoscale Assembly Line$() - check JEI for the exact parts before ordering anything.

Why a black hole? By the $(thing)Bekenstein bound$(), a horizon holds the most information any region of space can. Bekenstein and Hawking showed its entropy scales with horizon area, not volume. If anything can hold a universe in memory, it is this.

Three simulations, each gated by coil tier:$(li)a $(thing)stellar life cycle$() (tier 4)$(li)a $(thing)galaxy$() (tier 5)$(li)a whole $(thing)cosmology$() (tier 5)$(br2)Each run returns a huge spread of materials - and $(item)Horizon Shards$().
Last note on throughput: field emitter tiers multiply its parallels, just like every other multiblock. I keep looking into the lens and feeling it look back.

pages.name: Eye of the Event Horizon
pages.text: Cycling blocks: any of them fits (Interface Ports, higher coil/emitter tiers). Rotate, zoom and view layers in $(thing)JEI$().

$(thing)Machine data$(): a multiblock (16 item and 16 fluid inputs, 6 and 4 outputs).$(br2)$(thing)Makes$(): Cosmic String Segment, Cosmological Constant, Dark Energy, Degenerate Matter Chunk, Exotic Matter, Exotic Matter Crystal, False Vacuum, Graviton Crystal, Hawking Radiation, Heat Death Remnant, Horizon Shard, Inflaton Field, Liquid Metallic Hydrogen, Liquid Spacetime...
A sliver of event horizon brought back out of a simulated universe. Everything that falls into it is remembered.$(br2)Made in $(item)Eye of the Event Horizon$().
$(thing)Where these go$():$(li)$(item)Horizon Shard$(): Axiomatic Field Emitter, Cosmological Constant, False Vacuum, Graviton Crystal, Heat Death Remnant and more
